units.function: Filesystem test listing a desired Paperclip skill as missing and persistently installing it into Gemini Local's user skill home through a symbolic link.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent/Company adapter config supplies HOME and desired skill keys; the Gemini adapter inspects and mutates .gemini/skills, linking a Paperclip-owned source into a vendor runtime directory.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/company/adapter identity, HOME, desired skill key, persistent mode, missing/installed state and vendor skill symlink path.
units.lifecycle: A desired built-in skill is initially missing, sync creates a persistent symlink, and the returned projection reports it installed.
units.testAssessment: One happy path covers state transition and symlink materialization. Missing are path/symlink escapes, existing files/conflicts, permissions, concurrent sync, uninstall/rollback/update, source disappearance, version/hash/license/signature, tenant isolation, explicit host-owner approval and execution verification.
units.designRationale: Bridge Paperclip skills into a vendor CLI's native persistent discovery directory with minimal copying.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS Connector nodes need one trustworthy package lifecycle across vendors without each adapter independently owning installation policy.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE only. Make a Connector-node SkillPackageManager the canonical owner of signed/versioned install plans, host consent, paths, rollback and attestations; Gemini adapter contributes only a narrow target-directory/runtime activation driver.
units.responsibilityConflict: Caller-configured HOME is persistently mutated without a responsible host owner, approved package digest or rollback receipt. Installed state does not prove the skill is authorized for any Work or data scope.
evidence: 73eb2373 docs: use structured agent mentions in paperclip skill (#4103)
33353ce6 feat(skills): remove bundled paperclip-dev skill and retire required skill attribute (#7029)

units.function: Filesystem test listing a desired Paperclip skill as missing and persistently installing it into Pi Local's user Agent skill home through a symbolic link.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent/Company adapter config supplies HOME and desired skill keys; the Pi adapter inspects and mutates .pi/agent/skills, linking a Paperclip-owned source into a vendor runtime directory.
units.keyDataModels: Agent/company/adapter identity, HOME, desired skill key, persistent mode, missing/installed state and vendor skill symlink path.
units.lifecycle: A desired built-in skill is initially missing, sync creates a persistent symlink, and the returned projection reports it installed.
units.testAssessment: The single happy path mirrors Gemini almost exactly. Missing are path/symlink security, conflicts, permissions, concurrency, uninstall/rollback/update, provenance/signature, tenant/host ownership and proof of runtime activation.
units.designRationale: Use the vendor's native persistent skill directory while avoiding copied skill contents.
units.companyOsProblem: The same Skill package lifecycle must be canonical and vendor-neutral across Raft, Codex, DeepSeek, Gemini, Pi and enterprise Agents.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE only and do not create a second owner. Reuse the Connector-node SkillPackageManager contract; Pi-specific code is limited to capability discovery and an install/activate adapter with signed receipt.
units.responsibilityConflict: A symlink is installed into a user home from caller configuration without human consent, immutable package identity, permission/data contract or accountable evidence.
evidence: 73eb2373 docs: use structured agent mentions in paperclip skill (#4103)
33353ce6 feat(skills): remove bundled paperclip-dev skill and retire required skill attribute (#7029)
